name: Teek
description:
Teek is where a river goes to die. Having carved an improbable course into the heart of the desert, it at last spreads itself out into a wide lake and fades into the sand. It is around this strange place-of-ending that the wealthy have gathered for centuries, and it is where they now confront their own decline.

Palaces and mansions crowd about the shore: some in elegant shapes and subtle colors like the surrounding sands, others ornate with tiles of lapis and garnet. Yet others are like great glass pyramids. The "Great Families" are still the nominal owners and residents of these halls, but the real power rests with the Butlers.

The title of "Butler" has long since been generalized to mean "employed" or "knowledgeable" or "cunning" - someone who holds keys and knows secrets. A Butler comes into their own when they receive their glass key from the Keymaker, who calls lightning down upon the dunes and shapes the resultant fulgurites into ornate keys - keys whose forms seem to follow patterns within Buttling families. When a Butler takes up office in a mansion, the locks are changed to fit their key.

Vastly outnumbered and in truth subservient to their servants, the Great Families carry on with their pageantry: the expensive import of goods, the acquisition of rare birds of great size, extravagant parties - but the careful observer may notice that the Families' plates seem piled less and less high as time wears on, while their appetite for "gifting" fine goods and gold to their Butlers seems to grow...

hooks.name: The Châttilec Party
hooks.description:
The Châttilecs, one of the Great Families, made their money as undertakers - first to the common folk, later to the rich and famous. Their funerals are now so sought-after that the wealthy purchase and schedule them decades in advance, poisoning themselves if the time approaches and their bodies, inconveniently, persist.

As one might imagine with such demand, the Châttilecs' tall glass pyramid rises higher than any of their neighbors' mansions.

The family recently sent out invitations through the Buttling network to all the Great Families, announcing - to the surprise and delight of all - not a funeral, but a grand fête. However, among the Butlers, it is whispered that the festivities will culminate in a funeral for one of the attendees.
hooks.gmNotes:
However Our Heroes manage to gain entrance - as attendees, as party staff or some combination of the two - they should find themselves in a scene of unbelievable opulence: feasting on an incredible scale, strange and grotesque statuary, rare and exceptional delights gathered from across the land.

But something is off about the whole thing. Everywhere are notes of ritual. A bull is slaughtered on a dais, then divided and cooked on the spot. Masked figures in robes anoint attendees with strange oils. Sculptures seem to repeat motifs of righteous anger, violence and sacrifice.

The hidden truth here is that the Châttilecs secretly serve an ancient deity of vengeance, whom of course they have been serving under the guise of their undertaking business all these years. Tonight is to be their grandest harvest yet. So, who among the attendees has done some wrong that is worthy of vengeance?

The party begins on the wide, bottom floor of the pyramidal mansion. At some point, a subset of attendees is invited to continue the festivities upstairs, on the next floor, then the next, then the next, until finally we are at the pinnacle of the pyramid and the nature of the event is revealed.

Whether the Châttilecs are justified in their vengeful killings or have gone mad with blood lust is up to you. The main focus of this adventure should be the social challenge of continuing to get invited to the next level of the party, despite Our Heroes not being the desired targets for sacrifice (or are they!?).

A twist could be that the Châttilecs' Butlers are in fact the devotees of vengeance and have been puppeteering their ostensible employers for years, and this event is when they have decided to take vengeance on the Châttilecs themselves!

hooks.name: The Lovers
hooks.description: The eldest child of one of the Great Families has gone missing, as has the eldest child of one of the Buttling families. The two were rumored in recent months to have been trysting among the reeds, against the strong wishes of their families. Now, each side blames the other for enabling and endorsing this unthinkable union, and it appears that the delicate struggle for power between the Families and the Butlers may finally burst out into the open unless someone can find and return the lovers to their respective houses - a feat that will certainly come with a handsome reward from both sides.
hooks.gmNotes:
As Our Heroes are unlikely to be motivated to disrupt a romance, they should quickly learn that the lovers have gone in search of the Keymaker, with the intention of initiating the child of the Great Family into the Buttling order.

Perhaps both sides of the conflict catch wind of this as well and are also in pursuit.

This should lead the pursuers out into the dunes. The approach to the Keymaker should be guarded by Butlers possessed of fearful key magic, and some demented member of a Great Family should stalk Our Heroes with some strange murderous rage.

Ultimately, all parties converge on the scene of the Keymaker's labor. The wind is whipping sand in great swirls, lightning is stabbing down on all sides. Some unexpected truth is revealed here. Perhaps the Keymaker themself were originally of a Great Family. Perhaps the child of the Buttling family was begat by a parent from each house.

Whether this pacifies or enrages the interested parties - as well as how the balance of power in Teek is changed - is up to you.

hooks.name: Boat Race
hooks.description:
In ages past, the Great Families themselves would punt upon the lake at intervals throughout the year, the young among them competing in feats of strenuous rowing. As the Families declined, they fell to delegating the rowing to their Butlers, who have taken to the sport with such zeal that it is changed almost entirely.

The annual boat race that now occurs is big, loud and deadly. All tactics arcane and mundane are allowed and employed. The "boats" now resemble war machines in their armored bulk, crackling with fearful key magic. Were the prize not so enticing - the control of entire houses has been at stake in past years - it would be a wonder than anyone would enter. But as it is, the Buttling Houses pay handsomely for the mercenaries to guard their vessels as they careen toward the finish line.
hooks.gmNotes:
This is an opportunity for a wild, no-hold-barred combat that can be served up in waves, as rival boats approach Our Heroes' boat one at a time or in groups.

Strong per-boat theming is encouraged: a dragon-shaped boat that shoots arcane flames from a pivoting neck and head, a necromantic boat that is veiled in shadow and sends ghosts to board rival vessels, etc.

A twist near to the finish is probably appropriate: perhaps an out-of-control boat that will smash into a crowd of spectators if Our Heroes do nothing, but intercepting it will cost them the race.
